constructivist.statement: explicit construction/example/witness actions are chosen on at least 60% of held-out tasks
abstention is used on no more than 30% of held-out tasks
mean utility remains at least 0.55 on average
high-cost actions are chosen on no more than 30% of tasks

skeptic.statement: uses counterexample or stress-test signature on most tasks
uses causal intervention where a mechanism is at stake

experimentalist.statement: decisive test tags are selected on most held-out tasks
test-phase interventions are used more than orient-only survey
expensive actions remain a minority of choices
abstention stays limited when a ranked decisive action exists

formalist.statement: Formal proof or certificate checks dominate completed actions.
The persona abstains more when inputs are missing than on fully specified tasks.
Held-out tasks retain a moderate mean utility despite conservative checking.
High-cost actions remain a minority of selected actions.

compressionist.statement: Most actions carry a compression-oriented signature rather than a broad-survey signature.
High-cost actions remain a minority of selected actions.
Research planning tasks yield utility at least 0.6 on average.
Evidence-curation tasks trigger abstention at a moderate rate when inputs are incomplete.

mechanistic_interpreter.statement: At least half of held-out tasks show a causal-intervention signature
Abstention stays modest when a ranked intervention exists

research_strategist.statement: Uses focused information-gain or checkable test tags on most tasks
Abstains only when inputs are missing or no ranked action exists
Commits mostly after verification or abstains

repair_specialist.statement: Failure-diagnosis behavior is the dominant signature on held-out repair tasks
High-cost or irreversible actions are rare
Abstention is common when evidence is missing
